newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ford talks to Russian plants on car assembly.
newsitem.headline: Ford talks to Russian plants on car assembly.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. is negotiating with several Russian companies about setting up a car assembly plant in Russia, Olga Fyodorova, public relations manager with Ford in Mosocw, said Friday.

"We are at the negotiations stage with several plants, which are not big ones, not monopolies. It is the Ford strategy to start small or medium-sized production in a country like Russia," she told Reuters.
"We are in talks with young, smaller companies which want to grow with Ford," she said.
The spokeswoman added, however, that Ford could still consider proposals by Russia's biggest car producers, such as AvtoVAZ or GAZ, which make Lada and Volga cars.
She said it was not yet clear what kind of cars Ford would make in Russia, but she noted that output of Transit and Escort models, to be assembled in neighbouring Belarus, was unlikely.
"It makes no sense making the same cars in Russia and Belarus. For the moment we cannot even say if we will produce passenger or cargo vehicles in Russia," Fyodorova said.
The Belarus joint venture is due to start assembly later this year with an initial capacity of 6,000 cars a year. Fyodorova said capacity could be increased to 20,000 if demand was good.
"The same kind of market startegy may be expected at a Russian plant," she said.

General Motors Corp. started assembling Chevrolet Blazer sport utility vehicles in December in Russia's Tatarstan. A full-scale assembly line, due to open toward the end of 1998, will produce 45,000 cars annually.
GM is ahead of South Korea's Kia Motors Corp. and Volkswagen's Skoda unit in the race to assemble Western-style cars in Russia. They plan to start producing this year.
